newsitem.title: UK: Expectations of broad-based EMU recede - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Expectations of broad-based EMU recede - JP Morgan.

text.p: Market expectations of a broad-based European monetary union, including Italy and Spain, receded last week, according to JP Morgan's EMU calculator.
In the past five trading days, market prices indicated that the perceived probabilities of Spain, Sweden, Italy and Denmark joining EMU in 1999 all slipped.
Spain fell 4.0 percentage points to 74 percent, Sweden fell 1.0 point to 65 percent and Italy was down 2.0 points to 63 percent.

The decline follows reports during the week that Germany and the EU plan to offer a deal to Italy involving a delay of two or three years to its entry into EMU. These reports were denied, but come against a background of a hardening of the German government's vocal stance against a broad-based start to EMU.
According to the calculator, the assigned probabilities of Italy and Spain joining EMU on time have both dropped 8.0 points each over the past month and Sweden is down 13 points.
Elsewhere the probability of Denmark taking part in EMU in 1999 fell 5.0 points to 37.0 percent while the UK rose 8.0 points to 46.0 percent.
The market still believes there is a 100 percent chance of France and Belgium joining in 1999, which was the same as last week, the calculator showed.

JP Morgan's EMU calculator derives from interest rate swaps. The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
